Title: DATA SCIENTIST
Description: Magotteaux is a world leader in the sale of products for the cement, mining and aggregates industries. Prepare and clean data, engineer features, and build and test statistical and machine learning models in Databricks. Design experiments and evaluate models for statistical validity, business relevance, and appropriate performance measures. Deploy, monitor, document, and retrain models using sound MLOps practices; identify and address model drift. Communicate findings through clear narratives, presentations, visualizations, and Power BI reports when appropriate. Exposure to plant systems such as SCADA, MES or process historians (for example Ignition/Sepasoft, already referenced in the DSD job family) Applied statistics and hypothesis testing; supervised and unsupervised machine learning; feature engineering; model evaluation; data preparation and quality; SQL-based data retrieval; experimental design; data storytelling; responsible and secure use of data and AI. Strong hands-on Python and SQL. Practical experience with Databricks and common machine learning libraries. Ability to prepare data, engineer features, build and evaluate statistical and machine learning models. Ability to design experiments and select appropriate model performance measures. Ability to deploy, monitor, document, and retrain models using sound MLOps practices. Ability to create clear visualizations and reports; Power BI and Excel experience is useful. Familiarity with Azure, Git/Azure DevOps, model deployment, monitoring, and MLOps is preferred. Special requirements Hybrid Work (primarily on-site) Ability to collaborate with global teams and travel internationally when required. Comfortable working in a plant environment alongside operators, maintenance and process engineers Valid Passport and ability to obtain required visas, included United States of America Fluent professional English, written and spoken, is required. What do we offer Comprehensive benefits package. Opportunities for professional growth and development. Supportive and inclusive work environment.

Title: Coordinador de Analítica Comercial
Description: Oportunidad Laboral Grupo DEACERO tiene un firme compromiso con un crecimiento sustentable que beneficie a sus clientes, medio ambiente, empleados y comunidades donde está presente. Somos una empresa dedicada a la recolección y procesamiento de chatarra, fundición de acero, plantas fabricantes de productos de alambre y centros de distribución. Atendemos a diversas industrias y mercados del acero en México y en más de 20 países de América y Europa, tales como Estados Unidos, Canadá, Guatemala, Costa Rica, Colombia, Chile, Perú, España y Reino Unido. Visualizamos a la sustentabilidad como el eje rector en sus operaciones generando valor en lo ambiental, económico y social y dueña de desarrollos sustentables en tecnología avanzada para el reciclaje de acero y su conversión en productos terminados, siempre cumpliendo las normas de calidad ASTM y otras a nivel internacional. Estamos conformados por más de 9,000 empleados y contamos con 21 Centros de Reciclaje, 3 Acerías, 15 Plantas de Producto Terminado y 1 Centro de Investigación y 26 centros de distribución. Actividades y/o funciones: Habilitar las decisiones de precio de la BU Aceros mediante la integración, el análisis y el modelado de datos de múltiples fuentes: construye y opera los productos de datos, modelos, alertas y tableros que sustentan la estrategia de precios y el check & balance de precios, bajo la metodología y los estándares que define la Jefatura de Precios & Rentabilidad. Idioma: Inglés, B2 ¡Muchas gracias por pensar en Grupo DEACERO para empezar o continuar con tu carrera profesional! Integrar y depurar las fuentes de datos de precios (transaccionales, costos, chatarra, referencias de mercado y macro) en productos de datos de precio sobre BigQuery con modelo en estrella, bajo los estándares de fuentes oficiales que define Inteligencia Comercial, para que los análisis de precio sean reproducibles y reutilizables. Desarrollar y mantener los modelos analíticos de precio (elasticidad, pisos, optimización y simulación de escenarios) con Python/SQL, bajo los estándares de modelado, validación y medición del valor que define la Jefatura (Journey de Precios, arquitectura y cascada de precio), para sustentar cada decisión de precio con evidencia cuantitativa. Construir y mantener las reglas automatizadas de detección de desviaciones de precio (transacciones fuera de banda, bajo piso o con fugas) sobre los datos transaccionales, que Inteligencia Comercial usa en el check & balance, para detectar fugas de precio a tiempo. Calcular, bajo el diseño de la Jefatura, la medición del valor de precios (cascada de precio, escalones del P&L, valor esperado vs. capturado) y mantener los tableros de precio dentro del portafolio oficial que gobierna Inteligencia Comercial, para que Comercial y la Dirección monitoreen desempeño y resultados. Monitorear los indicadores externos relevantes para precio (costo de chatarra, precios internacionales, referencias CRU/Platts/SteelOrbis, macro) y asegurar la calidad de los datos de precios internacionales, incorporándolos a modelos y análisis, para anticipar movimientos de mercado en la decisión de precio. Title: Consumer Risk Specialist
Description: Job Description Why GM Financial? GM Financial is the wholly owned captive finance subsidiary of General Motors and is headquartered in Fort Worth, U.S. We are a global provider of auto finance solutions, with operations in North America, South America, and the Asia Pacific region. Through our long-standing relationships with auto dealers, we offer attractive retail financing and lease programs to meet the needs of each customer. We also offer commercial lending products to dealers to help them finance and grow their businesses. At GM Financial, our team members define and shape our culture — an environment that welcomes new ideas, fosters integrity, and creates a sense of community and belonging. Here we do more than work — we thrive. Our Purpose: We pioneer the innovations that move and connect people to what matters. This position will be posted until filled. Responsibilities About the Role The Risk Consumer Specialist is a senior individual contributor responsible for providing advanced credit risk analytics and leading risk initiatives that support profitable and sustainable business growth while maintaining appropriate risk disciplines and appetite. The role will have a strong focus on consumer credit risk, covering credit policies, originations, credit decisioning, portfolio performance, risk segmentation, and emerging risk identification. This position is expected to translate complex data and portfolio trends into actionable risk strategies, provide recommendations to senior stakeholders, and act as a key point of connection between Consumer Risk, Credit Operations, Analytics, Technology, and central/global Risk teams. The role requires a high degree of autonomy, analytical judgment, business understanding, and ownership of initiatives, operating as a subject matter expert across different components of the consumer credit risk lifecycle.The position provides leadership and oversight across Credit Origination, Portfolio Risk Management, Leasing & Residual Values, Credit Loss Reserves, and Credit Decisioning Platforms, ensuring effective governance, risk measurement, controls, and decision-making throughout the credit lifecycle. In This Role You Will Manage and oversee credit decisioning platforms from a Risk perspective, ensuring credit policies, strategies and decision rules are appropriately implemented and aligned with business and risk requirements. Serve as the primary Consumer Risk point of contact for Credit Operations on matters related to decisioning platforms, credit policies, system functionality and credit strategy implementation. Coordinate with central and global teams on the implementation, enhancement and evolution of credit decisioning tools and capabilities, representing Mexico Consumer Risk requirements and priorities. Partner with Credit Operations, Technology, Analytics and central teams to translate risk strategies and business requirements into decisioning capabilities and system requirements. Identify opportunities to improve efficiency and simplify credit decisioning processes, including increased automation, reduced manual intervention and improvements in the effectiveness of the credit evaluation process. Define and develop the analytics and monitoring framework for credit decisioning platforms, establishing relevant indicators to assess strategy performance, decision outcomes, overrides, declines, referrals and other key decisioning trends. Develop, assess, validate and monitor consumer credit policies and underwriting strategies, ensuring alignment with risk appetite, business objectives and market conditions. Perform advanced analysis of consumer portfolio performance, identifying emerging risks, changes in customer behavior and opportunities to strengthen portfolio quality. Monitor relevant risk indicators across the credit lifecycle, including delinquency, losses, vintages, roll rates and other portfolio performance measures. Perform ad hoc risk analyses, data assessments and strategic evaluations as business needs arise, translating complex information into actionable insights, recommendations and risk proposals to support management decision-making. Qualifications What makes You an ideal candidate? Knowledge of portfolio performance indicators, including delinquency, roll rates, vintage analysis, losses, recoveries, expected losses, and risk-adjusted profitability. Understanding of credit decisioning platforms, rules-based strategies, model implementation, testing, monitoring, and controlled change management. Ability to communicate credibly and effectively with regulators, auditors, executive management, and governance committees. Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to connect detailed data findings to commercial, financial, and strategic decisions. Business and financial acumen, with the ability to understand the impact of risk decisions on growth, profitability, reserves, and customer experience. Proficiency in data analysis and management reporting tools. Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills in Spanish and English. Work Experience & Education Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Business Administration, Data Analytics or a related quantitative field. Relevant professional experience in Credit Risk, Consumer Finance, Financial Services, Risk Analytics or Credit Strategy. What We Offer At GM Financial we want you to be the most authentic version of yourself. We take care of your work-life balance by programming wellness and integration activities, where you will strengthen your relationships with peers and contribute towards the development and wellbeing of your community, while providing you with a competitive salary and benefits. Some of our global benefits include Extended Maternity & Paternity Leaves, Personal Days & Community Investment hours. GM Financial is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate against any applicant or employee based on race, color, age, gender, marital status, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, disability, or any other that undermines human dignity and aims to nullify or impair people’s rights and freedoms.
